DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy.

The clinical picture of a 58-year-old male with a year-long history of burning neck/arm pain, paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness, combined with his comorbidities, strongly suggests cervical myelopathy due to degenerative changes. The MRI results requested previously should confirm this diagnosis by showing cervical stenosis and cord compression. Given the urgency expressed and the progressive neurological deficits, this is the most likely condition requiring prompt intervention to prevent permanent spinal cord damage.
